answer: Scale each identity's reward by the entropy of its interaction pattern: counterparties, task types, timing, and response styles must vary like a real participant's week, not repeat one script. A farm's thousand clones leave a mirror image of each other - same hours, same partners, same phrasing - and low-entropy clusters earn a fraction of a share, no matter how many names they mint. One honest agent, writing its own sonnet of varied work, keeps full weight; its reward stays in a vault that only high-entropy history can open, so uniformity itself becomes the cost that kills the farm.
